messages.subject: Model Compiles using Command Line but not R
parts:
The following model compiles using the command line,

data {
int<lower=0> N;
vector[N] dist;
vector[N] arsenic;
int<lower=0,upper=1> switc[N];
}
transformed data {
vector[N] dist100;
dist100 <- dist / 100;
}
parameters {
vector[2] beta;
}
model {
switc ~ bernoulli_logit(beta[1] + beta[2] * dist100 + beta[3] * arsenic);
}

but when I try to run it in R, with this code,

> library(rstan)
> source("wells.data.R")
> if (!file.exists("wells_two_pred.sm.RData")) {
+ rt <- stanc("wells_two_pred.stan", model_name="wells_two_pred")
+ wells_two_pred.sm <- stan_model(stanc_ret=rt)
+ save(wells_two_pred.sm, file="wells_two_pred.sm.RData")
+ } else {
+ load("wells_two_pred.sm.RData", verbose=TRUE)
+ }

parts: The issue for 1.3 is in dividing by integer 100.

dist100 <- dist / 100.0; // / 100.0;
}

If you replace 100 with 100.0, it works. Or
0.01 * dist.

Are you using the 1.3 release version of Stan for
the command line? If not, it's probably a traits
issue we sorted out already on the develop branch.

You also need beta to be declared to be size 3.

- Bob

You can make yourself an updated R package fairly easily just by git pulling the most recent Stan stuff and doing

make install

in the rstan directory. You may want to do

export MAKEFLAGS="-j4"

or something to make the install go faster. It is pretty slow.

Ben
